question: Which body was formed by Gandhi on 24 February 1919 to oppose the Rowlatt Act?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyagraha Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyagraha Sabha** was founded by **Mahatma Gandhi** on **24 February 1919** to oppose the **Rowlatt Act**.
 
• The **Rowlatt Act**, enacted in **1919**, allowed the colonial government to detain individuals suspected of sedition without a trial. It was perceived as a direct attack on the civil liberties of Indians.
 
• The **Satyagraha Sabha** was formed to organize protests and promote non-violent resistance (Satyagraha) against the unjust law. The Sabha served as a platform for spreading awareness and mobilizing the masses against the Rowlatt Act.
 
• Gandhi believed in the principle of **Satyagraha**, which emphasized non-violence and truth as a means to oppose injustice. The Sabha was one of the first concrete steps toward a nationwide movement against British colonial policies.
 
• The formation of the Sabha marked the beginning of a more organized and large-scale resistance by Indians against the oppressive colonial regime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rowlatt Act:**

 
 
• The **Rowlatt Act**, also known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, was passed by the British Government to curb growing nationalist activities. It gave the government extensive powers to arrest and detain individuals without trial.
 
• The Act faced widespread opposition as it suppressed civil liberties such as freedom of expression and the right to legal representation. It led to significant unrest and protests across the country.
 
 
 
• **Satyagraha Movement:**
 
 
• **Satyagraha** is a concept of non-violent resistance developed by Mahatma Gandhi. It involves using truth and non-violence as tools to fight injustice and oppression.
 
• The **Satyagraha Sabha** was an organization created to implement and spread the principles of Satyagraha across India. It played a crucial role in mobilizing masses against British policies.
 
• The movement also included boycotts, non-cooperation, and peaceful protests to challenge British authority.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations:**
 
 
• **Congress Committee:** This refers to the Indian National Congress, the principal political organization that led India's independence movement. However, it was not specifically formed to oppose the Rowlatt Act.
 
• **Swaraj Sabha:** This organization was part of the broader nationalist movement but was not directly connected to the Rowlatt Act protests.
 
• **Khilafat Committee:** This was a separate movement initiated to protest against the British dismantling of the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I. It was not related to the Rowlatt Act.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**

 
 
• The protest against the **Rowlatt Act** culminated in the infamous **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** on **13 April 1919**, where British troops under General Dyer opened fire on unarmed civilians in Amritsar.
 
• This tragic event significantly intensified the Indian freedom struggle and led to greater participation in Gandhi's non-cooperation movement.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Satyagraha Sabha:**
 
 
• The principles of non-violence and truth advocated by the **Satyagraha Sabha** became the cornerstone of India's freedom movement.
 
• It inspired future movements such as the **Non-Cooperation Movement** (1920), the **Civil Disobedience Movement** (1930), and the **Quit India Movement** (1942).
